title: Proactive trace-linked incident initiation with PagerDuty scheduling
creator: Ravi Singh
description: Summary: Build a system that can proactively open and schedule incidents in PagerDuty when a correlated tracing signal indicates an impending or ongoing service degradation. The system should attach relevant trace snippets, metric snapshots, and a candidate runbook to the PD incident; it should also allow operators to defer/acknowledge with one-click Slack actions and reschedule follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: 1) When trace anomaly detector fires for a service, a PagerDuty incident is created with a synthesized summary and a trace link. 2) The incident contains structured attachments: top 3 traces, key metric deltas, and suggested runbook link. 3) PagerDuty schedule fields are set so on-call rotation is respected. 4) Slack incident channel gets a message with buttons: Acknowledge, Run Runbook, Assign Owner, Defer. 5) UI shows auditable created_by and confidence score. 6) System passes security review and load tests for 200 incidents/hour.
design_notes:
- Tracing hook: add an outbound enrichment pipeline that, on positive anomaly, samples top N traces, runs lightweight root-cause scoring, and constructs a concise incident summary.
- PD integration: use Events API v2 to create incidents on behalf of the Redwood integration account; map service->PD-service mapping stored in config. Include custom PD payload with links to console trace viewer and metric snapshot URL.
- Scheduling: consult PagerDuty schedules API to infer active schedule for the service; if no match, fall back to team-default schedule. Add optional manual override in Console.
- Slack actions: use block kit buttons tied to internal webhook endpoints. Actions trigger: acknowledge incident (PD API), inject runbook steps into thread, or open a short live-remediation checklist.
- Runbook suggestion: match on service tag and recent failure signature; attach the top-ranked runbook draft and note confidence score.
- Rate limiting & deduplication: incidents deduped by signature hash for 15 minutes to avoid noise. Implement backoff and sampling thresholds to prevent PD throttling.
- Observability: increment counters for automated incidents created, PD API errors, deduped incidents, and average time-to-ack from automation.
non_goals:
- Not building full incident commander UI (out of scope).
- Not replacing manual incident creation flows.
- Not automating remedial code rollouts.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): prototype trace summarizer and PD event creation in staging; validate PD schedule lookup. Phase 2 (Core, 2 weeks): implement dedupe, Slack actions, runbook suggestions, security review. Phase 3 (QA & Load test, 1 week): run chaos scenarios and simulate burst incidents. Phase 4 (Canary rollout, 1 week): enable on a low-traffic service, monitor false positives and PD rate. Phase 5 (Rollout & Docs):  gradual enablement and runbook curation.
Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/pd-automation, spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs/pull/487
security_considerations:
- PD events will be sent using a scoped integration token stored in KMS; ensure token rotation policy.
- Attachments must not leak PII; trace scrubbing lambda removes user identifiers and request bodies.
- Audit log: every auto-created incident must write an immutable audit entry with reason and confidence score.
- Security review required for PD token usage and data attachments.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for trace summarizer and signature hashing.
- Integration test: end-to-end incident creation against PD test account.
- Load test: simulate 250 anomaly events/minute to validate PD API rate handling and queueing behavior.
- False positive test: run historical replay against last 90 days of traces and measure precision/recall.
rollout_strategy:
- Canary on service: 'verification-gateway' for 72 hours with auto-disable on >3 false positives/day or PD errors >1% of requests.
- Observability: dashboards for automated_incidents/sec, pd_api_errors/sec, avg_time_to_ack_by_source.
- Operator controls: Console toggle per-service, PD schedule override, manual suppression window.
docs_and_commms:
- Docs: console guide, admin runbook for disabling automation, public-facing FAQ for customers.
- Internal comms: send plan to SRE and Oncall channels and schedule a walkthrough demo.
- Training: 1-hour demo with oncall teams during rollout week.
postmortem_and_metrics:
- If a false auto-incident causes an outage or unnecessary escalation, run a postmortem linked to the PD incident and tag ENG-43718 as parent.
- Success metrics: reduce mean time to detection by 20% and mean time to acknowledge by 15% for covered services.
- Track false positive rate, incidents created/day, and operator override frequency.
